messages.text: Taurus Bay dents some lofty reputations in Rising Stars

metadata.summary: Harry Redknapp could have another top prospect on his hands after Taurus Bay made a winning chasing debut in the Boodles Rising Stars Novices’ Chase at Aintree.
metadata.content: Taurus Bay dents some lofty reputations in Rising Stars | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Taurus Bay dents some lofty reputations in Rising Stars The top guns were stumped in the Rising Stars Novices’ Chase at Aintree on Saturday as Taurus Bay made the perfect start to his chasing career with a hard-fought success over Talk To The Man. Saturday 7 November 2026 16:12, UK Image: Taurus Bay (right) ridden by Ben Jones goes on to win the Boodles Rising Stars Novices' Chase at Aintree Harry Redknapp could have another top prospect on his hands after Taurus Bay made a winning chasing debut in the Boodles Rising Stars Novices’ Chase at Aintree. A lot of the pre-race chatter revolved around Paul Nicholls' No Drama This End making his eagerly-awaited fences bow and he was sent off the 8-11 favourite. However, Ben Pauling's five-year-old was a more than useful hurdler in his own right last term and always seen as more of a chasing prospect. With No Drama This End's tank flashing empty on the run to the last it was left to Ben Jones on board Taurus Bay to outbattle the match-fit Dan Skelton runner Talk To The Man after the last, edging a one-and-a-quarter-length verdict at odds of 13-2. messages.text: Verstappen fastest in final practice but faces grid penalties with Ferraris

metadata.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen was fastest in final practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix but will serve grid penalties along with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP: Max Verstappen fastest in final practice but faces grid penalties with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP: Max Verstappen fastest in final practice but faces grid penalties with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc Max Verstappen was quickest from Kimi Antonelli in final practice in Brazil but will start at the back for Sunday's race; Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc also have penalties; watch Qualifying later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5pm), live on Sky Sports F1 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Saturday 7 November 2026 15:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen goes fastest in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix final practice Red Bull's Max Verstappen was fastest in final practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix but will serve grid penalties along with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc. Verstappen pipped new Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli by 0.025s but will start at the back of the grid for a complete power unit change , while Hamilton and Leclerc have 10-grid place penalties for exceeding their internal combustion engine allocation. Mercedes had already announced on Friday that George Russell will have a five-place penalty for a new internal combustion engine, the second time he has exceeded that part's limit, while the Ferrari drivers are being penalised for the first time, so have a bigger penalty. messages.text: Hamilton, Verstappen, Leclerc with Sao Paulo GP grid penalties

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc will all serve big grid penalties for engine changes at Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP grid penalties: Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc to drop down Interlagos grid | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP grid penalties: Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc to drop down Interlagos grid Both Ferrari drivers to take 10-place demotions, while Red Bull's Max Verstappen to head to back of grid; George Russell already has penalty; rain forecast for race day; watch Sao Paulo GP Qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 5pm on Sunday live on Sky Sports F1 Saturday 7 November 2026 16:02, UK Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc will all serve big grid penalties for engine changes at Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Ferrari team-mates Hamilton and Leclerc will both take 10-place demotions for the use of fifth international combustion engines this season, one more than is permitted. They will start no higher than 11th on Sunday's race grid. And Verstappen will start at the back of the 22-car grid after taking three different fresh engine components on his Red Bull.
